extracted.intended_audience: extramural researchers, research administrators, NIH staff, and institutional grants offices
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Office of Extramural Research (OER) mission, responsibilities, policies, systems, and initiatives that govern NIH extramural research administration, compliance, peer review, data sharing, workforce support, and security. The page summarizes the standards and programs OER uses to guide applicants, recipients, and NIH staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide corporate framework for NIH research administration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Extramural Research (OER) provides the corporate framework for NIH research administration, ensuring scientific integrity, public accountability, and effective stewardship of the NIH extramural research portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OER oversees activities related, but not limited to, high-profile digital platforms, grant compliance, peer review, communications with the extramural community, scientific misconduct, human subjects protection, and laboratory animal welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide authoritative resources for all phases of NIH extramural research funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide authoritative resources for the corporate framework for all phases of NIH extramural research funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include eRA, NIH Guide to Grants and Contracts, NIH Data Book; OER supports the recipient community and the 24 NIH Institutes and Centers by providing policy, guidance, systems, and other support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement and inform infrastructure, policies, processes, and procedures enabling NIH extramural programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement and inform infrastructure, policies, processes, and procedures that enable the execution of NIH extramural research programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: Funding Opportunities, staff training, Loan Repayment Program, SBIR/STTR; OER develops and maintains systems and processes that enable program execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure integrity and compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the integrity of and compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and policies that govern NIH extramural research funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific areas cited: awards oversight, research misconduct, peer review integrity, clinical trials, animal welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and enhance policies/programs supporting a diverse biomedical research workforce
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop, assess, and enhance NIH policies and programs that support the training, career development and education of a diverse biomedical research workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts should incorporate analyses of national workforce trends and needs and include programs that help early stage investigators (e.g., Katz Award, Pathway to Independence, NIH Director's New Innovator Award).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide authoritative policy resources (including Peer Review Policy and eRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide authoritative resources including Policy, Peer Review Policy, Administration Systems (eRA), NIH Guide for Grants and Contracts, Animal Welfare Assurances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These resources are the canonical references for applicants, recipients, and NIH staff when interpreting and applying extramural policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and inform central websites, reporting tools, and outreach channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement and inform central websites on NIH funding, programs for the innovator community, reporting tools and transparency (RePORT), Extramural Nexus (News), and outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OER develops and curates web resources and communications to guide applicants, recipients, and staff on policies, opportunities, and transparency tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure research integrity and safe/respectful workplaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure integrity and compliance across domains including Research Integrity and Safe and Respectful Workplaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OER works on preventing and addressing misconduct, harassment, discrimination, and breaches of ethical or professional standards in the research environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify the peer review framework to focus on highest-impact research
rubrics_metrics.description: Working collaboratively to simplify the peer review framework for research project grant applications so reviewers focus on the identification of the strongest, highest-impact research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives include mitigating the effect of reputational bias and reducing reviewer burden; this implies review criteria and procedures should emphasize impact and reduce procedural complexity for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement the Scientific Data Management and Sharing Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accelerate implementation of the Scientific Data Management and Sharing Policy, including development and deployment of comprehensive resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OER developed the Scientific Data Sharing website to provide information and resources for applicants, recipients, and NIH staff on NIH scientific sharing policies; compliance guidance and educational resources are part of this effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address integrity threats such as misconduct, confidentiality breaches, and inappropriate foreign influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Address integrity threats due to research misconduct, breaches of peer review confidentiality, inappropriate foreign influences, harassment and discrimination in the scientific workplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OER activities include detection, prevention, policy development, and response measures to protect the integrity of NIH-funded research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement foreign disclosure and risk management provisions for SBIR/STTR
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement foreign disclosure and risk management provisions of the SBIR and STTR Extension Act of 2022, requiring federal agencies to establish a due diligence program to assess security risks posed by applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OER leads efforts to operationalize statutory due diligence requirements for small business applicants to identify and mitigate security risks associated with foreign connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide robust security systems for grants administration (two-factor authentication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide robust security systems to support grants administration, including implementation of two-factor security requirements via Login.gov or an InCommon Federated account through which users authenticate and access external eRA modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security and authentication requirements are enforced for access to grant administration systems to protect applicant and award data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance reduction of administrative burden with preservation of research integrity for animal research
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to implement provisions of the 21st Century Cures Act, such as to reduce administrative burden associated with laboratory animal research programs while at the same time preserving the integrity and credibility of research findings and the protection of animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy changes should streamline administrative requirements but not compromise scientific validity or animal welfare protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize funding and programs to support early stage investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead efforts to ensure the future biomedical research workforce by focusing NIH attention on increasing the numbers of early stage investigators it funds and fostering programs that support career transition and innovative research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of programs: Katz Award (requires no preliminary data), Pathway to Independence Award (support transitioning from graduate school to faculty positions), NIH Director's New Innovator Award (supports innovative, high-impact projects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide education and outreach to the extramural community
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide diverse education opportunities and resources to the extramural research community through major events and multimedia channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Virtual NIH Grants Conference and preconference events, Data Management and Sharing webinar series, YouTube Grants Channel, All About Grants podcasts, Extramural Nexus, LinkedIn, and X; metrics cited include attendee and view counts to demonstrate reach.
